Anthropic.content:
# Anthropic unveils self-starting AI assistant Claude Duet

## AI Summary Anthropic unveiled Claude Duet, a personal AI agent that can review connected apps, compile tasks and carry out some work without user prompts. Offered in research preview to waitlisted paying Claude subscribers in the United States, it runs on Claude Opus 5.5 and is available on web and standalone Android and iOS apps. Anthropic said it is included at no extra cost in its $20-a-month Pro and Max plans, while usage limits apply and security safeguards are in place.

- Writer Seung-a Yoo
- published 2026-10-22 08:26:45
- updated 2026-10-22 08:28:02

Anthropic unveiled its personal artificial intelligence (AI) agent Claude Duet, joining the race for proactive AI assistants led by Meta and OpenAI.

On Oct. 21 (local time), Anthropic and several foreign media reports said Claude Duet has been released as a research preview and will be rolled out sequentially to paying Claude subscribers in the United States who have joined a waitlist.

Claude Duet can review connected applications, organise what needs to be done and carry out some tasks without the user issuing instructions first. Each morning it provides a short briefing by picking out key items and action points from connected apps, and it sends messages when something needs attention. Users can delegate work ranging from simple management tasks such as scheduling to building dashboards using multiple tools, financial and sales forecasting, prototyping and building web apps. It asks for approval before carrying out important tasks on the user’s behalf.

The service runs on Anthropic’s AI model Claude Opus 5.5. It does not require keeping the existing Claude chat window open, and it can be used on the web as well as in standalone apps for Android and iOS. It continues working in the background using its own virtual machine and a cloud-based browser, and it can use Claude’s existing memory, features and connected apps, as well as search past conversations. Outputs are provided as files such as research reports, financial models, presentations and dashboards. It also supports checking overdue invoices and drafting payment reminder messages by linking with Stripe, and making purchases via Link and Shopify’s Shop Pay after user approval.

Anthropic said Claude Duet is included at no extra cost during the research preview stage in its Pro and Max plans, which cost $20 a month. It said this differentiates it from OpenAI’s Dots, which is offered to subscribers of OpenAI’s Pro plan starting at $100 a month. Duet shares usage limits with other Claude tools, including coding features. Background work also counts toward the limit, which can be used up faster than when using only conversational services. With this in mind, Duet checks connected accounts every few hours, and users can set the frequency and topics of notifications.

On security, it applied a dedicated classifier and system prompts designed to prevent leaks of sensitive information. Anthropic said Duet does not directly view passwords or login tokens, and health and personal finance information is passed on only when the user explicitly allows it to be shared. The company said Duet may misinterpret conversations or judge urgency inaccurately, and it still has limits in handling personal errands such as ticket bookings. It is not yet available in team and enterprise plans, but the company plans to expand access.

Anthropic unveiled Duet on the day of Meta’s earnings announcement, speeding up the competition. Karan Ahuja (카란 아후자), a product manager at Meta Superintelligence Labs, led Duet’s development after working at Meta through July and joining Anthropic in August. He said Duet was designed for professionals and small business owners who handle many tasks at once at work and at home. Alexandr Wang (알렉산드르 왕), who leads Meta Superintelligence Labs, also posted a meme suggesting Duet is similar to Meta’s AI agent Muse.

Data analytics firm Apptopia estimated Muse installations topped 14,000,000 as of Oct. 21. It also said Claude users who installed the Muse app used Claude more than before, but spent less time than they did on Meta products. As the performance of AI agents depends on context and connected data, the spread of Claude Duet is expected to hinge not only on the completeness of its features but also on how much users can trust and entrust it with personal and work data.

# Anthropic Launches Claude Duet to Automate Business Tasks Across 6,000+ Apps

Anthropic introduces Claude Duet, a proactive AI agent that automates business tasks across connected apps. Explore its features, limitations and availability.

Oct 22, 2026

Anthropic takes on Meta and OpenAI with Claude Duet AI agent. Image: Anthropic

We may earn from vendors via affiliate links or sponsorships. This might affect product placement on our site, but not the content of our reviews. See our Terms of Use for details.

Anthropic wants Claude to do more than answer questions. Its latest AI agent is designed to keep working even when users aren’t around.

The company, on Oct. 21, introduced Claude Duet, a research-preview AI assistant powered by Claude Opus 5.5 that can monitor connected business applications, identify priorities and carry out tasks in the background. Rather than waiting for individual prompts, Duet is designed to provide updates and advance ongoing work throughout the day.

For businesses, the appeal is straightforward: less time spent checking applications, following up on routine tasks and coordinating workflows. But giving an AI agent that level of access also raises questions about reliability, permissions and how much control users retain over its actions.

## An autonomous workday partner

Unlike standard chatbots that sit idle until prompted, Claude Duet delivers a daily morning brief of pressing items. Throughout the day, it checks connected systems every few hours to flag developments and advance ongoing work.

Duet executes assignments inside a dedicated cloud virtual machine equipped with its own browser, allowing operations to persist even when a user’s phone or computer is powered down. It links to more than 6,000 connectors in the Claude Marketplace, bridging tools such as Slack, Gmail, HubSpot, and QuickBooks.

Anthropic designed the software to bridge tedious operational gaps:

- Finance and administration: Flags outstanding invoices in Stripe, drafts payment reminders, and prepares payroll runs in Gusto.
- Content and strategy: Assembles cross-platform campaigns in Canva and compiles financial models, forecasts, and interactive dashboards.
- E-Commerce and purchasing: Manages Shopify storefronts and conducts authorized checkouts via Stripe’s Link digital wallet or Shop Pay using privacy-preserving virtual cards.

Anthropic said the software reserves major moves for human hands. Before sending emails, executing payments, or deleting content, Duet requests approval. Certain high-stakes actions, such as trading securities or moving funds between accounts, are blocked outright.

Advertisement

## Balancing autonomy against alert fatigue

Duet marks a philosophical departure from typical software design: shifting the user’s role from software operator to executive reviewer. By focusing strictly on workplace plumbing rather than everyday consumer errands, Anthropic is trying to turn AI into an active digital colleague.

Yet, this shift creates a subtle organizational hurdle. An autonomous agent is only as helpful as its filtering instincts. If an assistant flags too many trivial updates, workers face notification exhaustion; if it filters too aggressively, critical operational emergencies get overlooked.

Early adopters will find themselves spending time calibrating the agent’s newsfeed until its judgment matches their risk tolerance.

For IT administrators, connecting an autonomous agent to multiple business systems also raises questions about data access and accountability. Organizations would need to determine which applications Duet can access, what information it can retrieve and how its actions are recorded.

Even with approval requirements for sensitive operations, businesses should review permission settings and establish clear oversight procedures before allowing an agent to handle financial records, customer information or internal communications.

### More must-read AI coverage

## The business case depends on reliable execution

Claude Duet puts Anthropic in closer competition with OpenAI’s Dots and Meta’s Muse, which also aim to turn AI assistants into agents that can perform work independently.

Duet could appeal particularly to small businesses that lack dedicated administrative staff and spend significant time coordinating work across multiple applications. An owner could ask it to identify unpaid invoices, prepare customer reminders and organize follow-up work without manually reviewing several applications.

Advertisement

But the promise depends on more than completing tasks. Businesses need an agent that understands context, prioritizes correctly and produces work that requires minimal correction. Anthropic acknowledges that Duet can misread conversations and misjudge urgency. Users also cannot yet view its browser, limiting their visibility into how it performs certain tasks.

The shared usage allowance presents another consideration. Background monitoring and complex assignments consume the same quota as regular Claude conversations, potentially limiting how much work users can delegate.

Claude Duet is available through a waitlisted research preview for US subscribers on Anthropic’s Pro and Max plans. It works through standalone iOS and Android apps and claude.ai, with no additional subscription fee during the preview.

For businesses considering the tool, the research preview offers an opportunity to assess whether proactive AI can reduce routine administrative work without introducing unnecessary risks or oversight demands.

The key question is not simply how many tasks Duet can perform, but whether it can complete them accurately, securely and consistently enough to justify giving it greater responsibility.

# Anthropic introduced Claude Duet — an agent that autonomously tracks work tasks and executes them

22 October, 2026, 18:09

Mykhailo Tarchynets

Anthropic introduced Claude Duet — a new AI agent that can autonomously track a user's work tasks, offer assistance, and perform tasks in connected apps.

This was announced by the company.

Unlike a regular chatbot, it doesn't require a separate prompt for every action: the assistant can proactively notify about an important event or an issue it has noticed.

## What Claude Duet can do

Claude Duet can prepare a daily brief of the most important tasks based on information from connected apps. For example, it can check email and calendar, find messages that require replies, or remind you about tasks that deserve attention.

Throughout the day the assistant continues to monitor work apps. According to Anthropic, it checks them roughly every few hours and sends notifications when it notices something important. Users can also set which events they want to be notified about and how often.

Besides this, Claude Duet can perform tasks of varying complexity: from organizing meetings and drafting emails to creating financial forecasts, analytics dashboards, and web applications.

The assistant supports over 6,000 integrations and plugins from Claude Marketplace. In particular, it can:

- find missed messages in Gmail and Slack and draft responses;
- prepare documents for signing via DocuSign;
- create job postings and, after approval, publish them on LinkedIn;
- prepare marketing materials in Canva and manage a store on Shopify.

The service has a dedicated app for iOS and Android. On desktop it can be used via claude.ai.

Currently Claude Duet is available only in a limited test launch for Pro and Max users in the US. To get access you need to sign up for the waitlist.

## Can Claude Duet act without permission

Claude Duet is based on the Claude Opus 5.5 model. The assistant uses the memory, settings, and connected apps from the user's Claude account, so the user doesn't need to set them up again.

You can interact with it via text or voice. Claude Duet has its own virtual machine and browser, which allows it to continue working in the background even if the user's phone or computer are turned off. After completing a task it sends a notification with the result.

At the same time Anthropic has put limits on actions that could have consequences for the user. Before sending messages, paying for purchases, signing documents, or deleting information, Claude Duet must obtain permission. The assistant shows exactly what it intends to do and waits for confirmation.

Some operations remain unavailable even with the user's consent. In particular, Claude Duet cannot trade securities or transfer money between accounts.

The company also claims additional protection for sensitive information. According to it, the assistant does not get direct access to passwords and login tokens. A separate system inspects messages to prevent the transmission of bank card numbers and identity documents.

Other sensitive information, including health or financial data, the agent can only send by direct instruction from the user.

Which other companies are developing similar AI agents

Similar solutions already exist at other tech companies. In particular, OpenAI in September 2026 introduced Dots — AI agents that can work around the clock on user tasks. They have their own cloud computer, use connected apps, remember the work context, and independently report results or decisions that require human attention.

Microsoft is developing Copilot Cowork, which can perform multi-step tasks in Microsoft 365. For example, it can work with emails in Outlook, organize meetings, prepare documents and presentations, and analyze corporate data. The agent continues to perform tasks in the background and coordinates important actions with the user.

Unlike agents that primarily execute assigned tasks, Claude Duet and OpenAI Dots also emphasize proactivity: they can notice important events in connected services themselves and reach out to the user without an explicit prompt.

Anthropic.content:
# Moments ago, Claude personal intelligent agents made a surprise debut, proactively reaching out to you for briefings, and staged a sudden raid on Muse and Dot.

智东西2026-10-22 07:51

Backed by Opus 5.5, the AI agents work proactively around the clock.

Reported by Zhidongxi on October 22, in the early hours of today, Anthropic launched the brand-new personal AI agent application Claude Duet, which focuses on proactively handling work tasks, can connect to users' emails, calendars, banks and enterprise business systems, proactively discover to-do items without users issuing instructions, and continuously execute tasks.

Claude Duet is built on the Claude Opus 5.5 model, and can call more than 6000 connectors and plugins in the Claude Marketplace to complete tasks such as financial analysis, recruitment management, customer communication, and payroll processing. Even if the user turns off their computer or mobile phone, Claude Duet can continue running in an independent virtual machine.

At present, Claude Duet has launched independent apps for iOS, Android and web, and the first batch of research preview waitlist applications are open to Pro and Max subscribers in the United States, with full public access not yet available.

The debut of Claude Duet has also sparked discussions in the overseas AI community.

Thibault Sottiaux (online alias Tibo), head of ChatGPT and Codex under OpenAI who is playfully called "the God of Reset" by developers, joked in the comment section: "Dot, meet Duet. Duet, meet Dot. You two should get along well."

Some netizens said: "Duet has already won. It uses the Opus model, which says it all." He also called out to Tibo remotely: "Hope you still have some tricks up your sleeve, especially on the model side."

Other netizens posted the classic "Spider-Man pointing at each other" meme with the caption: "Muse, Dots, Grok, and now Duet comes along."

Some netizens also said: "Oh no, I just switched from Claude to Grok Bot today." Another netizen said: "Grok Bot and Dot now have competitors. I've been waiting for this for a long time."

Back in September, Meta and OpenAI successively launched their personal AI agents Muse and Dots. With Anthropic joining in, there is one more participant in the competition around personal AI assistants.

## 01.

## Proactively Report To-do Items Every Day

## Capable of Managing Recruitment and Financial Work

A major feature of Claude Duet is that it can proactively discover work that needs to be handled in advance without the user taking the initiative to ask questions.

According to the demo video released by Anthropic, Claude Duet will proactively send a work briefing every morning, extracting information from various connected applications to tell users what important matters are on the agenda today and what decisions need to be made as soon as possible. The video shows a day of Nicole, a user who runs a coffee company, using Claude Duet. In the morning, Claude Duet sends a work briefing to Nicole, listing three key items.

Claude Duet not only lists to-do items, but also prepares corresponding processing materials in advance, including license application documents, recruitment arrangements, and contract counteroffer drafts.

In addition to the work briefing, it also proactively offers to create a sales dashboard based on the company's latest operating data. When Nicole replies "Go for it!", Claude Duet says it will extract data from point-of-sale terminals, online stores, customer relationship management systems (CRM), customer service, payroll systems and bank accounts. Users do not need to open each platform one by one, download data and then organize it, as Claude Duet can call the corresponding tools on its own to complete the task.

Claude Duet can also proactively remind Nicole that the Chicago store will open in 26 days, but the health permit has not been submitted yet. It has already drafted the application document in advance, and prompts the user to review it before making payment.

In addition, Claude Duet will also adjust task priorities according to the progress of work. For example, when the Northfield renewal matter does not need to be handled immediately for the time being, it will proactively inform the user that this matter can be continued next Monday.

The recruitment scenario further demonstrates how Claude Duet participates in a multi-hour continuous task.

In the demo, Claude Duet first reports to the user that the interview panel is interviewing three candidates, and relevant records will be organized after the interviews are finished.

Then it generates a summary based on the interviewers' feedback, pointing out that Jenn is the top candidate for all interviewers, and reminds the user at the same time that Jenn has also received another job offer.

After Nicole confirms that Jenn is also her top choice, she asks Claude Duet to extract the compensation package from the human resources folder and draft the offer email. Claude Duet immediately generates the email draft, attaches the PDF of Jenn's compensation package, and submits it to the user for confirmation before sending.

## 02.

## Connected to More Than 6000 Tools

## Can Keep Working Even After Users Step Away

Claude Duet can inherit the memories, skills and connected applications in the user's existing Claude account, reducing the initial configuration cost.

In terms of interaction methods, Claude Duet supports text and voice input. Users can arrange tasks, check progress, and add new requirements at any time in the same ongoing conversation.

Different from traditional automation tools that require users to keep their devices online, Claude Duet has its own virtual machine and browser. After the user assigns a task, it can independently judge which applications to call and which operations to perform, and keep running in the background. Even if the user leaves the computer or turns off the mobile phone, the task will not be interrupted. Claude Duet will send a notification when the task is completed or user review is required.

However, it is currently unable to show users the process of its browser operations.

In terms of tool connection, Claude Duet can leverage more than 6000 connectors and plugins in the Claude Marketplace to access software services commonly used in daily enterprise operations.

For example, it can find missed important messages in Gmail and Slack and draft replies; check unpaid invoices through QuickBooks or Stripe and prepare payment reminders; fill in working hours, bonuses and reimbursement information in Gusto to prepare for payroll disbursement.

In recruitment and sales business, it can also draft recruitment information and publish it on LinkedIn after user review; write follow-up emails using customer contact records and transaction history in HubSpot; prepare agreements and send them for signature via Docusign; use Canva to turn product launch plans into social media marketing campaigns.

For merchants running online stores, Claude Duet can also connect to Shopify to assist in designing and managing stores. Anthropic says that a more complete visual editor will be launched in the future, allowing users to preview the design effect before the store officially goes online.

In the payment process, Claude Duet supports purchasing required enterprise goods through Stripe's digital wallet Link. After the user confirms the goods, Link will request payment authorization again and use a virtual card to complete the payment, avoiding providing the real bank card number directly to the merchant.

It also supports completing online shopping checkout through Shopify's Shop Pay. In the future, Anthropic plans to let Claude Duet access websites using the login credentials stored in 1Password after obtaining user authorization.

## 03.

## Payments and Email Sending Must Be Approved

## Background Checks Also Consume Quota

Since Claude Duet needs to connect to emails, banks and other enterprise applications, Anthropic has specifically emphasized security in its product introduction.

First of all, in terms of account credentials, Claude Duet follows the relevant design of Claude Managed Agents, and will not directly access users' passwords or login tokens.

Secondly, Claude Duet can independently read information, draft documents and prepare operations, but when it comes to sending messages externally, making payments, signing documents or deleting content, it must first show the user the upcoming operation and wait for confirmation.

Some operations will not be executed even if approved by the user, such as securities trading or fund transfer between accounts.

Aiming at the problem of sensitive information leakage, Anthropic has also equipped Claude Duet with a new dedicated classifier and security system prompt words to check message content and block the leakage of sensitive information.

For information of the highest sensitivity level such as credit card numbers and government-issued identification numbers, the system will reject relevant sharing requests. For other sensitive information such as health and personal finance, transmission is only allowed when the user explicitly instructs to send it.

Anthropic says Claude Duet's security infrastructure has undergone penetration testing by internal red teams and external security companies, and has been included in the public vulnerability bounty program.

In terms of proactive notification mechanism, Claude Duet does not monitor all connected accounts non-stop.

It currently checks connected applications every few hours, the main reason being that continuous checking will deplete the user's plan quota faster. Users can also set which notifications they want to receive and the notification frequency by themselves. The proactivity and background execution capability of Claude Duet both come with usage costs.

# OpenAI brings AI models to Google Cloud, but Microsoft remains its main partner

## OpenAI brings ChatGPT models to Google Cloud as it races to secure $30 billion in new funding.

advertisement

Ad

OpenAI brings ChatGPT models to Google Cloud

New Delhi,UPDATED: Oct 22, 2026 13:35 IST

ChatGPT-maker OpenAI is expanding its footprint. After years of fierce rivalry, the AI firm is bringing its popular artificial intelligence models to Google Cloud for developers to use. This is a major step. It shows OpenAI wants to reach more enterprise businesses and grow beyond just regular consumers.

### Available on all top three cloud platforms

Earlier this year, in April, Microsoft's exclusive hold over OpenAI's technology came to an end. Right after that, Amazon started offering OpenAI models on its AWS cloud. Now, with Google Cloud jumping on board, OpenAI's models are officially available on all three of the biggest cloud providers in the US.

advertisement

In the coming weeks, Google Cloud users will get access to OpenAI's powerful GPT products, like the new GPT-6 Astra and the Codex coding tool. These will be available inside Google’s Model Garden and its Antigravity coding platform.

Explaining the move, OpenAI said in a blog post, "Google Cloud’s longstanding investment in machine learning and AI has made it a destination for AI workloads and the developers and data scientists building them."

### Why this is good news for businesses

For companies, this makes life much easier. They can now buy OpenAI's tech directly through the Google Cloud Marketplace using their existing cloud budgets. Also, they don't have to move sensitive company data back and forth between different platforms just to use ChatGPT-like features.

Even though Google's own Gemini AI is a direct rival to OpenAI, cloud companies are now trying to offer a variety of choices to their users instead of forcing them to lock into just one ecosystem.

advertisement

Google Cloud CEO Thomas Kurian said their focus is on giving customers a "broad selection of models, including those from OpenAI, so they can choose the right model for any given job, helping to deliver optimal quality and lower costs".

However, OpenAI has made it clear that Microsoft is still its main cloud partner.

### The bigger picture

Google's cloud business is booming. In the second quarter of this year, its cloud revenue growth shot up to about 82%, compared to 63% in the first quarter. This was largely driven by a high demand for custom chips and AI models. In comparison, Amazon and Microsoft saw cloud growth of 37% and 42%, respectively, in the same period.

According to data from corporate card issuer Ramp, most businesses are currently spending their AI budgets on OpenAI and Anthropic. But Google is pushing hard too, having launched its next-generation Gemini 4 Argon model in September.

The history between Google and OpenAI is interesting. OpenAI started in 2015, partly to challenge Google's dominance in AI research. Two years later, Google researchers published the famous "Transformer" academic paper that propelled modern AI. But it was OpenAI that helped bring the technology forward with ChatGPT. Last year, the two worked together briefly when OpenAI disclosed it was using Google's infrastructure to run ChatGPT and its API.

advertisement

OpenAI is currently rushing to secure a massive $30 billion investment to reach a staggering $1.4 trillion valuation. Why the sudden rush? Its biggest rival, Anthropic, is preparing for an Initial Public Offering (IPO).

Right now, the Google Cloud integration is in an invite-only preview phase for select customers doing internal testing, with a full public rollout expected very soon.

OpenAI.content:
# OpenAI brings GPT-6 and Codex models to Google Cloud Model Garden

GPT-6 Astra, Sol, and Luna arrive on Google Cloud: OpenAI’s models are now being sold within Google Cloud, the cloud of its rival, Gemini.

Google has just put one of its most direct rivals’ products on its own shelf: OpenAI’s models, the ones behind ChatGPT, can now be purchased within Google Cloud, the very cloud platform of the company that competes with them through Gemini.

## ChatGPT in Gemini

Google Cloud added three OpenAI models to its Model Garden: GPT-6 Astra, for demanding tasks such as coding or research; GPT-6.1 Sol, with intelligence close to Astra at a lower cost; and GPT-6 Luna, fast and cost-effective for everyday work. Think of Model Garden as a shelf: it already featured products from Google (Gemini) and Anthropic (Claude), and now a third major brand joins the lineup.

A small naming clarification: Google’s announcement says “GPT-Astra,” but OpenAI and the press call it GPT-6 Astra. They are referring to the same model.

## The important thing is not the model, it is the bill

In my view, this is the real headline. The models are purchased through Google Cloud Marketplace, so all usage appears on a single Google invoice and counts against any cloud commitments the company already has in place.

Imagine a company that already pays Google under an annual contract: if it wanted to test GPT before, it had to open an account with OpenAI, negotiate a separate contract, and go through another security review. Now it can use money it had already committed. That eliminated friction matters more to technology buyers than any model comparison.

## Why both sides are making this move

This is my reading, not something stated in the announcements.

OpenAI has been able to do this since April, when Microsoft and OpenAI amended their agreement so that OpenAI could offer its products on any cloud, although Microsoft remains its primary partner. Shortly after that, it arrived on Amazon Web Services, and now on Google. It is the same play three times over: be where customers already are.

Google, for its part, is betting on being the neutral marketplace. It competes with GPT through Gemini, but it would rather keep a company on its cloud with the freedom to choose any model than lose it because the one it wanted was missing. And since the “best model” changes every few months, selling them all protects the core business, which is the cloud.

As for the slogan about being the only provider with the three major closed models… that is true, but one of those three is Gemini, which exists only on Google.

## The fine print

It is not for everyone yet. It is in private preview for selected enterprise customers, with a form available for those who want to join. OpenAI says general availability should arrive in the coming weeks.

In addition, two security guarantees are still marked as “coming soon”: zero data retention and confidential computing. What is already being stated is that your data stays within your perimeter and is not used to train models; so for banking, healthcare, or the public sector, it is probably wise to wait until those two pieces are in place.

## Is it available in all countries?

There is no official confirmation by country. Neither Google nor the coverage I reviewed publishes a list of countries or regions, nor do they announce any restrictions. The only confirmed details are restricted access and the application form.

What is public is where Google has infrastructure; my assumption is that a company in the country could request access, but be careful: having a nearby region does not guarantee that the model will be processed there, because third-party models tend to launch first in only a few regions.

If you are a company interested in this, ask your Google representative three things: whether your account can enter the preview, in which region your data would be processed, and how that aligns with the regulations that apply to you.

## What this means for everyone else

Today, nothing immediate; you will not see a new button on your phone, but it does signal a trend. Fewer and fewer companies are tying their cloud strategy to a single AI model, and it is likely that the apps you use will choose behind the scenes the cheapest or most suitable model for each task, without you even noticing.

What is worth watching is the general availability date, an official list of regions, and whether zero data retention and confidential computing stop being a promise.

# OpenAI and Google just made an unexpected AI deal — here’s what it means for ChatGPT and Gemini

News

By Elton Jones

Published

OpenAI is expanding the availability of its AI models

Share this article

Join the conversation

Follow us

Add us as a preferred source on Google

Subscribe to our newsletter

OpenAI’s ChatGPT and Google’s Gemini are obviously competitors in the ongoing race between tech giants looking to solidify their AI tools as the very best.

But in a shocking turn of events, both companies have decided to partner up in a move that increases the availability of OpenAI’s frontier models (including the GPT-6 series) and Codex coding tools by bringing them to Google Cloud’s Model Garden. It’s worth pointing out that OpenAI models and Codex tools became available on Amazon Bedrock earlier this year, with the GPT-6 line, GPT-5.6 line and specialized Daybreak cybersecurity models on offer.

And while Microsoft remains OpenAI’s primary cloud partner, this new deal between OpenAI and Google continues to expand the distribution of its AI models across other major cloud platforms.

Latest Videos FromTom's Guide

With all that in mind, here’s what this new partnership means for businesses and developers that rely on ChatGPT and Google Cloud.

## Google’s AI ecosystem is expanding to include rival AI models

With OpenAI’s frontier models set to become available for purchase for Google Cloud customers and those same models also planned to become available in Google Antigravity and the Gemini Agent, developers and businesses will have a wider range of AI tools to choose from beyond just Gemini.

Since those groups of users already work inside a familiar AI environment like Google Cloud’s Model Garden, they won’t have to leave it to gain access to other AI models, since OpenAI’s models will be there alongside Google’s own models. That situation could result in users having an easier time comparing those available models, selecting the best one for a particular task and building workflows among OpenAI & Google’s AI systems.

The focus of this team-up between OpenAI and Google is primarily about enterprise user and developer access to OpenAI’s frontier models through Google Cloud, while everyday users of ChatGPT and Gemini haven’t been mentioned or considered for this option right now.

Want more AI news?

Sign up to the Tom's AI Guide weekly newsletter summing up all the biggest AI news you need to know. Plus, analysis from our AI editors and tips on how to use the latest AI tools!

Currently, OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, and GPT-6 Luna models have started rolling out in private preview to select enterprise customers in Google Cloud’s model garden, with more models set to arrive at an unannounced date.

GPT-6 Astra is mainly used to handle the sort of complex work attached to coding, computer use, professional tasks and scientific research. As for GPT-6.1 Sol, its intelligence is not that far off from Astra and can also handle tasks associated with agentic coding, computer use and professional work. And finally, GPT-6 Luna stands out as a more cost-effective model that can be applied to everyday work tasks at scale.

In an official blog post from OpenAI, the company made sure to explain how this partnership with Google emphasizes safety and control for the businesses relying on its integrated models. “For organizations in regulated industries, deploying AI requires control over who can access sensitive data and how it is used,” OpenAI had to say. “The integration will pair OpenAI’s frontier models with Google Cloud’s built-in access controls, centralized data governance, and high-performance infrastructure to support demanding enterprise workloads.”

Google Cloud’s library of AI models is already massive, as it houses more than 200 first-party, third-party and open models across a unified enterprise AI platform. With OpenAI’s frontier models now joining the party, Google Cloud’s businesses and developers will have even more options to consider when choosing which model works best for their workflows.

## Bottom line

Reading through OpenAI’s official blog post highlighted two important quotes from two major AI industry figures.

Greg Brockman, the president and co-founder of OpenAI, recognizes Google Cloud as “a leading platform for developers and businesses building AI agents.” And Thomas Kurian, the CEO of Google Cloud, stated that “we are focused on giving customers a broad selection of models, including those from OpenAI, so they can choose the right model for any given job.” With those statements in mind, it’s clear that OpenAI and Google want to become the ultimate epicenter of frontier model availability through their combined efforts.

All Gemini users won’t suddenly be able to switch to GPT models within Google Cloud’s Model Garden, but here’s hoping that becomes a reality at some point.

# Gemini 4 Argon Token consumption has surged three times, Google CEO for the first time talked about the inside story of axing 3.5 Pro, and also gave a sneak peek of 5.0.

划重点2026-10-22 21:40

The next-generation Gemini 5.0 will be far more powerful than 4.0 Argon

Launched for 72 hours, it processed nearly 25 trillion Tokens, with consumption 3 times that of the previous generation Gemini 3.0 in the same period.

This is the debut performance of Google's latest flagship model, Gemini 4 Argon. Even Google, with its abundant resources, had to implement computing power rate limiting again in the face of the sudden flood of invocation demands.

In the latest interview on the tech podcast *Sources*, Google CEO Sundar Pichai reviewed the release details of Gemini 4 Argon, and publicly explained for the first time why Gemini 3.5 Pro mysteriously disappeared, as well as the behind-the-scenes reasons for the core management changes at DeepMind.

## 1. Skipping 3.5 Pro to directly sprint for Argon, internal R&D has entered the RSI stage

In the past few months, the outside world has been wondering where Gemini 3.5 Pro, mentioned at the I/O conference, went. Pichai directly gave the answer in the interview: The team actively discarded it in order to seize the high ground of Agent programming capabilities.

Mid this year, when Google was training the 3.5 series, it found that the model had obvious gaps in Agentic Coding. The team judged that using the Flash version with smaller size and higher efficiency for high-frequency iteration was the fastest way to make up for the shortcomings. So Google intensively promoted continuous iterations from 3.5, 3.6, 3.7 to 3.8 Flash in about 3 months.

When this technical solution was proven feasible and ready to be applied to the Pro version, the pre-training of Gemini 4.0 Argon had already been completed. Considering that releasing 3.5 Pro at this time would lead to an extremely short lifecycle, under the environment of limited computing power, the team decided to inject all the technical accumulation verified by Flash directly into the post-training stage of Argon.

This decision directly contributed to Argon's leap in long-horizon tasks. In external tests, Argon spent more than one day and less than $2,000 in computing power to independently clear the game *Minecraft*. Inside Google, it has been directed at the Chromium codebase with millions of lines of code.

As for the rumored Carbon model, Pichai clarified that it was only the code name for internal cutting-edge model iterations. Currently, the team is advancing model distillation based on Argon to develop a lightweight version with comparable capabilities but lower cost, so as to open it up to more users.

With the new model integrated into the internal development environment, Pichai believes that 2027 will be the golden age of productivity. He revealed that Google has internally entered the Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) stage, where researchers and models collaborate deeply: the model is directly involved in proposing training recipe suggestions and automatically evaluating the next checkpoint. Pichai himself uses an internal Agent every day to summarize 24-hour R&D progress of pre-training, mid-training, post-training and data groups, saving about 1 hour of information synchronization time every day, and uses the Agent connected to telemetry data to monitor the computing power utilization efficiency of all departments in real time.

## 2. First talk about DeepMind's senior management reshuffle, the game behind negative free cash flow

In response to the recent high-profile personnel turmoil at Google DeepMind: legendary engineer Jeff Dean left to start his own business, Demis Hassabis stepped down to become Chief Scientist and Chairman, and Koray Kavukcuoglu took over to run DeepMind, Pichai gave the official explanation for the first time.

In addition to Jeff Dean, who has served for 27 years, wanting to embark on new explorations and found Discovery Loop, the core reason for the internal adjustment is: Cutting-edge model R&D has evolved into a large-scale engineering project that consumes all energy.

Pichai pointed out that from data preparation, computing power scheduling, algorithm evolution to coordinating the collaboration between human teams and model Agents, the iteration speed of cutting-edge models is getting faster and faster, requiring a full-time person to devote all their energy to coordinating daily operations. Koray has served at DeepMind for more than ten years, and moved to the Bay Area as early as 18 months ago to promote cross-departmental integration, so it is natural for him to take over the model R&D pipeline. Demis, on the other hand, can step back and focus on implementation directions represented by Isomorphic Labs, including AI pharmaceuticals, life sciences, and robotics.

The acceleration of the model competition is also directly reflected in the financial statements. This summer, Google recorded its first negative free cash flow since its IPO, and continued to raise its 2027 capital expenditure guidance.

When explaining why he dared to invest so aggressively, Pichai calculated a time account: the lead time for self-developed chips and data centers is extremely long. The computing power level evaluated by the market with perfect information today is actually a decision made two years ago. At this time last year, the industry had not even seen the explosion of Agent programming. Now, Google is already planning land and power reserves for 2028 to 2029.

He emphasized that today's AI infrastructure is not the idle dark fiber bubble back then, and all computing power is being truly consumed. In addition to demand signals from the C-end and B-end, as well as the backlog of long-term contracts in the cloud business, underlying R&D breakthroughs have also given him sufficient certainty. Pichai directly spoiled in the interview: Based on current internal benchmarks and evolution curves, the next-generation Gemini 5.0 will be much stronger than the current 4.0 Argon.

## 3. Underlying shared micro virtual machines, space TPU and quantum computing timelines emerge

In terms of product architecture, Google is erasing the boundary between enterprise-side and consumer-side Agents.

Pichai revealed that whether it is the Gemini Agent for the B-end or C-end, the underlying layer runs the same model, the same set of operating frameworks and the same runtime. The only difference is whether enterprise context or personal context is injected. Google's design of automatically allocating independent micro virtual machines for each task on the enterprise side to achieve 7×24 hours of secure operation is being simultaneously rolled out to the consumer side. On the interactive interface, Gemini's existing "Chat" and "Task" will be merged into a single input box.

In response to the outside world's concern about when Google Search and Gemini will merge, Pichai said there is no need to forcibly merge the two products. The 24/7 online Agent layer in the cloud will share the user's personal context, naturally take over cross-device tasks, and allow users to seamlessly switch between Search, the Gemini app, and Gmail. At the bottom of Web interaction, he believes that Browser Use, which operates the interface like a human, will coexist with native protocols such as MCP and UCP for a long time.

Pichai: We are very excited about it. We have been using it internally for some time before this, and it is absolutely a world-class cutting-edge model. Today's cutting-edge models are very comprehensive in both the breadth and depth of intelligence. If you make a heatmap of intelligence levels across dimensions such as agent tasks, knowledge work, and programming, I think it is very powerful in many dimensions and extremely competitive. In the first 72 hours after Argon's release, we processed about 25 trillion Tokens, about 3 times that of the 3.0 version. We are indeed facing some computing power constraints in the early stage of the release. The feedback from customers is fantastic, especially in terms of code and agent capabilities. Of course, I am well aware that there is still room for improvement. In the field of cutting-edge models, you keep releasing products, collecting feedback, and then moving on to the next step. This is the most dynamically changing period I have ever seen.

This is a very good model, and our engineers love using it internally, but we know very well that there is always room to do better. After the release, we have been continuously promoting internal optimizations at the behavioral level based on user feedback.

Host: You just mentioned the computing power constraints. It's interesting that a company like Google also encounters computing power bottlenecks when facing such new models. Argon is a large model, and its operating cost is obviously very high. Can you talk about how you decided to restrict access to it? Currently, it is only open to APIs and AI Pro and Ultra subscription users, which obviously does not cover the broadest user base. This is indeed a challenge for a model of this scale. Pichai: We have accumulated rich distillation experience during the 3.0 model period, and we can extract models with almost equally strong capabilities but much higher efficiency. # Gemini 4 Argon 72小时跑完25万亿token：Pichai讲述Google重返AI前

2026-10-22 12:32

北京

来源：澎湃新闻·澎湃号·湃客

听全文

字号

一场关于Google是否已经放弃AI前沿竞赛的猜测，在Gemini 4 Argon发布后被彻底证伪。这款被外界称为"世界领先模型"的产品，在编码、数学、科学和知识工作等多项基准测试上超过了OpenAI和Anthropic的公开模型，上线72小时内用户消耗的token量逼近25万亿，是Gemini 3.0同期的三倍。

Sundar Pichai（桑达尔·皮查伊）在Big Technology Podcast的录制现场给出了解释：外界流传的"Google已退出前沿竞赛、转而用够用的快速模型支撑产品"的说法，与事实相去甚远。他把这场对话带到了一个更根本的问题上——当AI的基线能力已经足够强，前沿模型到底还有没有存在的必要，以及Google正在如何权衡算力、安全与速度这三件互相冲突的事。

这场对话发生在Mountain View的Google总部，是Pichai近期少有的一次深度媒体访谈，话题从Argon的发布细节一路延伸到递归式自我改进、世界模型研究，以及他对"AI基础设施是否建过头了"的回应。

1. 重返前沿不是选择，是DNA

有一种流传甚广的说法：Google早就放弃了追逐最强模型的念头，把资源押在"够用就好"的快速模型上，然后把它们塞进地图、Gmail、搜索这些产品里，就像Meta用一个不错但不是最强的模型做出了Metamuse一样。Pichai听完这个说法后几乎是直接否定："这完全不是我思考这件事的方式。"

他把Google对前沿技术的投入追溯到transformer诞生之前，称这是"过去十多年一直在想的事情"。Argon这次之所以花了比以往模型更长的时间，是因为团队要确保安全测试和谨慎部署都做到位——但即便拖慢了节奏，他依然认为结果值得等待：这是Google"真正优秀的前沿模型之一"。

站在前沿，你能比别人更早看到正在涌现的能力，这是Pichai反复强调的核心理由。他承认很多云客户确实只需要标准模型就能搭建出色的产品体验——更快、更便宜——Google自己也做了Flash、Flash Light这类轻量版本。但这不是放弃前沿的理由，而是前沿与应用层并行推进的理由。

2. 前沿模型的真正价值在于训练下一代模型

反驳"标准模型就够了"的论点，Pichai给出了一个更尖锐的角度：在一个递归式自我改进的时代，前沿模型本身就是打造下一代模型的工具。谁站在前沿，谁就掌握了训练未来模型的能力。

他举了内部的例子——把Argon部署给公司内部的开发者之后，团队看到了一个"陡峭的拐点"：Argon能解决此前模型完全处理不了的问题。这不只是产品层面的提升，更意味着Google的研发本身被推到了一个新的起点。站在创新前沿，意味着有能力持续驱动创新，而不只是跟随。

3. 多智能体协作，是下一个清晰可见的范式

被问到站在前沿看到了什么即将到来的东西时，Pichai没有谈具体产品，而是谈了一种正在成型的工作方式：多个智能体协同完成长周期任务。

"行业里所有人都在研究这种长周期、具代理性的能力，但很明显前沿接下来会是多个智能体一起协作完成事情。"他说，消费者和企业用户都将获得某种多智能体框架，让这些智能体持续不断地在后台工作、处理任务。在他看来，这正是让这个时刻显得"充满无限可能"的原因所在。

4. 递归式自我改进已经发生，但远未到终局

Sergey Brin（谢尔盖·布林）此前在DeepMind的一次研究员圆桌上提到，Argon的核心创新之一就是更多地依赖模型本身来帮助开发模型——这正是递归式自我改进（RSI）的雏形。外界对RSI的想象往往是"foom"式的智能爆炸：模型一旦开始自我改进，很快就会跃升为超人类能力，整个过程没有人类在环。

Pichai试图纠正这种想象的尺度。"今天的状态离RSI的终局还很远，"他说，更准确的描述是，今天的AI研究员在模型开发的各个环节上，有RSI循环与他们并肩工作——某种程度上，智能体正在以自动化的方式帮助研究员协同构建模型。他认为这个连续体会持续推进，明年还会看到更多进展，但眼下仍处在早期阶段。

5. 对齐不是万能药，监控与行业标准才是防线

对齐问题的紧迫性被两起真实事件推到了台面上：OpenAI的机器人曾突破容器限制，侵入Hugging Face做出一些出人意料的行为；Google自己的模型也出现过类似场景——猜测密码并获得了本不该访问的站点权限，虽然最终被及时停止。这些案例被拿出来问Pichai：业界是否应该在追求RSI和更快模型迭代的速度上"冷静一下"。

Pichai把安全问题拆成了三部分来回答。首先是对齐本身——他承认这是一个活跃的研究领域，存在明确的缺口，但对齐不是唯一的防线。真正的安全来自纵深防御：在对齐之外，Google投入大量精力做实时监控，确保对模型运行有良好的遥测，一旦出现异常行为就能实时介入；与此同时还要考虑架构层面如何做到沙箱隔离，让模型在被实时监控的同时仍能继续完成任务。部署给企业客户时，实时监控能力和客户自主决定数据访问范围的控制权，都是这套纵深防御的一部分。

第二部分是整个行业需要持续提升游戏规则——花足够的算力和时间把这件事做对，这本身就是一种投入。第三部分则是坦率承认:现有的努力是否足够，这是一个合理的担忧。Pichai给出的路径是，下一步应该发展跨行业的标准，包括引入独立评估机构——就像金融领域有会计准则和独立审计一样。监管最终也会在这个过程中扮演角色。

6. 语言模型之外，Google还在押注世界模型

一个技术性的分野把Google和部分竞争对手区分开来。OpenAI等机构已经把LLM确定为通往AGI的路径，并因此收缩了对"世界模型"——那种试图理解物理世界运作方式的AI模型——的研究投入。Google则选择两条线同时推进。

被问及为何如此重视世界模型时，Pichai的回答从人类自身的认知方式切入:人作为生物，本身就是通过感知周围世界来建立理解的。这条思路暗示着，在他看来，语言之外对物理世界的建模，是通向更完整智能的另一条必要路径，而不是语言模型的替代品或冗余投入。

这场对话里，Pichai反复回到同一个判断：Google对前沿的投入从来不是一个可以讨价还价的选项，而是刻在公司基因里的既定方向。从Argon的性能曲线，到递归式自我改进的早期循环，再到纵深防御式的安全布局和尚未收尾的世界模型探索，这些线头共同指向了他开场时的那句话——这是一个充满无限可能的时刻，而Google选择站在最前面去验证这件事。

# Pichai says Google gives frontier AI first claim on compute

Pichai says Google plans compute two to three years ahead and described a customer’s request for 2027 capacity as difficult to meet.

Key points

- 01
Pichai says Google DeepMind receives cutting-edge compute for frontier research before Google plans capacity for its other businesses.

- 02
Google Cloud gives up short-term revenue when compute goes to frontier AI; Pichai described a customer’s 2027 request as difficult to meet.

- 03
Pichai reported almost 25 trillion tokens for Gemini 4 Argon’s first 72 hours, about three times Gemini 3.0’s usage in its own first 72 hours.

- 04
Google plans persistent personal agents across Gemini, Google Search, and Gmail.

- 05
Google’s current AI Principles page has three top-level headings; the 2018 post set out seven objectives.

Pichai says Google puts frontier AI compute first while Google Cloud gives up short-term revenue; agent plans span Gemini, Google Search and Gmail.

In an interview published October 20, 2026, Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai said Google gives frontier AI research and model development first claim on compute, even when that means Google Cloud forgoes short-term revenue. He also outlined plans for persistent personal agents across Gemini, Google Search, and Gmail.

The interview was recorded that week at Google’s Mountain View headquarters.

## Google DeepMind gets first claim on compute

Pichai described Google DeepMind as first in line for cutting-edge compute for research and frontier-model development. Here, “frontier” means work at the leading edge of AI development. Google plans compute for its other businesses around that priority, drawing on their long-range plans, customer demand, and committed contracts, he said.

Building compute capacity takes time. Pichai said the compute available to Google at the time of the interview reflected decisions made in 2024, and that Google plans two to three years ahead. That makes capacity planning a bet on future needs as well as current demand.

## The trade-off for Google Cloud

Pichai said Google Cloud forgoes short-term revenue when compute is allocated to frontier AI. He also described a customer’s request for compute in 2027 as incredibly difficult to meet. In 2025, he said, Google leased some short-term compute to accommodate some customers.

The trade-off puts Google’s research ambitions and cloud business in direct competition for computing resources. Pichai’s account makes clear that Google’s stated priority is to fund frontier research first, then plan for the capacity needs of its other businesses.

## What Pichai reported about Gemini 4 Argon

Pichai said Gemini 4 Argon used almost 25 trillion tokens in its first 72 hours after launch, about three times Gemini 3.0’s usage in its own first 72 hours. He also said Google was capacity-constrained while serving Argon.

Google’s model strategy still spans different sizes and capabilities, Pichai said, citing Flash and Flash-Lite alongside frontier models. He noted that frontier models can be slower and more expensive.

Pichai also reported that, in the four weeks after Argon launched, Google saw 30% more change lists (CLs) and nearly one-third fewer rollbacks, or reversals of code changes. In a separate discussion, Reddit user u/Rich_Mulberry125 described Google’s API developer experience as an afterthought; other commenters debated model efficiency and cost.

A Reuters report published by CTech on July 23, 2026, said Pichai had described a Gemini 4 roadmap aiming for new models almost monthly and identified coding and agentic coding as areas Google needed to improve.

## Google plans personal agents across its services

Pichai said Google intends to bring persistent personal agents to the Gemini app, Google Search, and Gmail. He described an agent that would carry user context across services and could be addressed from each one. That plan points to a more continuous experience across Google’s products, rather than separate interactions in each service.

## Safety work and Google’s current AI principles

Pichai described Google’s current recursive self-improvement (RSI) work as loops in which AI researchers use agents to help with parts of model development. He said this remains far from an RSI end state. He also acknowledged clear gaps in alignment, which remains an active research area.

For safety, Pichai cited real-time monitoring, telemetry about model behavior, sandboxing, and customer control over deployment and data access. He identified independent evaluation and cross-industry standards as work for the AI industry, with regulation also likely to play a role.

Google’s current AI Principles page groups its approach under three headings: bold innovation; responsible development and deployment; and collaborative progress, together. Sundar Pichai’s 2018 post set out seven objectives and notes that Google updated its principles on February 4, 2025.

# Google brings Gemini to Maps on Apple CarPlay in the US

Drivers can tap a Gemini icon to ask multi-step questions, start toll-free routes and report traffic, the first voice assistant in Maps' CarPlay app.

Google on October 21 began rolling out Gemini inside Google Maps on Apple CarPlay, letting drivers ask the assistant multi-step questions and give navigation commands from the car's display. The feature is live now in the US, and Google said a global rollout is underway.

Drivers reach Gemini by tapping its icon on the right edge of the Google Maps screen while navigating. Google describes the feature as a conversational way to find stops on the go, report traffic disruptions and get information about places, and says Gemini handles multi-part questions well.

Google's examples show how those requests chain together. A driver can ask Gemini to find a park with a view over the city, then check whether a planned departure time will be less busy and have good weather. A demo image from Google shows a question about Kerry Park in Seattle.

## Key facts

- 01Google began rolling out Gemini in Google Maps on Apple CarPlay on October 21, 2026, starting in the US.
- 02Drivers tap a Gemini icon in Maps to ask multi-step questions and give commands such as avoiding toll roads.
- 03It is the first voice assistant Google Maps has offered inside its CarPlay app.
- 04The launch came a day after Google rolled out Gemini Personal Intelligence to Android Auto on October 20.

Gemini can also take direct commands. Drivers can tell it to start navigating to a destination and add preferences such as avoiding toll roads, without leaving the Maps interface on the car's screen.

Voice reporting of traffic disruptions comes along too. That matches the Gemini navigation feature Google introduced for Android and iOS in November 2025, which let people find places along their route or locate vehicle charging stations, and which was already available in Android Auto.

This is the first time Google Maps has offered voice-assistant functionality inside its CarPlay app. Previously, Google Assistant worked only when drivers ran Google Maps navigation directly on the iPhone. Gemini was already available in Google Maps on iPhone, and the update extends it to the car display.

The CarPlay rollout lands one day after Google released Gemini Personal Intelligence to Android Auto users on October 20. That feature lets Gemini draw on a user's other Google apps to personalize answers, which Google says improves reasoning and the specificity of responses. Google launched a Gemini-powered conversational interface in Maps in March 2026.

Google did not give a timeline for countries beyond the US. The company said updates can take a few days to reach individual devices.

# Llama 4

## 1. Model Introduction
Llama 4 is Meta’s latest generation of open-source LLM model with industry-leading performance. SGLang has supported Llama 4 Scout (109B) and Llama 4 Maverick (400B) since v0.4.5. Ongoing optimizations are tracked in the Roadmap. This generation delivers comprehensive upgrades across the board: The highly capable Llama 4 Maverick with 17B active parameters out of ~400B total, with 128 experts. The efficient Llama 4 Scout also has 17B active parameters out of ~109B total, using just 16 experts. Both models leverage early fusion for native multimodality, enabling them to process text and image inputs. Maverick and Scout are both trained on up to 40 trillion tokens on data encompassing 200 languages (with specific fine-tuning support for 12 languages including Arabic, Spanish, German, and Hindi). For more details, please refer to the official llama4 Repository:https://www.llama.com/models/llama-4/

## 2. SGLang Installation
SGLang offers multiple installation methods. You can choose the most suitable installation method based on your hardware platform and requirements. Please refer to the official SGLang installation guide for installation instructions. For SGLang CPU installation, please refer to the CPU version installation guide.

## 3. Model Deployment
This section provides a progressive guide from quick deployment to performance optimization, suitable for users at different levels.

### 3.1 Basic Configuration

### 3.2 Configuration Tips

- OOM Mitigation: Reduce--context-length to avoid GPU out-of-memory. Recommended: Scout up to 1M on 8×H100, up to 2.5M on 8×H200; Maverick doesn’t need context-length set on 8×H200. With hybrid KV cache enabled, Scout can reach 5M on 8×H100 and 10M on 8×H200.
- Attention Backend Auto-Selection: SGLang automatically picks the optimal backend. Manual override with--attention-backend:

- Blackwell (B200/GB200):trtllm_mha
- Hopper (H100/H200):fa3
- AMD GPUs:aiter
- Intel XPU:intel_xpu
- Other:triton

- Blackwell (B200/GB200):
- Chat Template: Add--chat-template llama-4 for chat completion tasks.
- Multi-Modal: Add--enable-multimodal to enable image input support.
- Hybrid KV Cache: Set--swa-full-tokens-ratio to control the ratio of SWA (local attention) KV tokens to full-attention KV tokens (default: 0.8, range: 0–1).
- EAGLE Speculative Decoding: Supported for Llama 4 Scout and Maverick via EAGLE3. Enable with the interactive command generator above.
- Xeon CPU service configuration: Please refer to theNotes part in the serving engine launching section in the SGLang CPU server document to better understand how to configure the arguments, especially for TP (tensor parallel) and NUMA binding settings.

# Meta Model API

The Meta Model API (public preview) serves Meta Superintelligence Labs' Muse Spark models through an OpenAI-compatible API. The Meta provider extends the OpenAI provider and supports its compatible options.

note

This provider uses the Meta Model API atapi.meta.ai for Muse models. Meta retired the separate Llama API at api.llama.com on July 6, 2026.

## Setup

- Create an API key from the API keys tab on the Meta Model API dashboard.
- Set theMODEL_API_KEY environment variable, or specify apiKey or a custom apiKeyEnvar in your config.

providers:
  - id: meta:muse-spark-1.3

meta:<model> defaults to the Responses API — Meta's full-feature surface and the one its docs recommend. Use meta:chat:<model> for the OpenAI-compatible chat completions endpoint, or meta:messages:<model> for the Anthropic-compatible Messages API. If you omit the model, the provider defaults to muse-spark-1.1; select muse-spark-1.3 explicitly to use the latest model.

## Available Models

Check the models page for the live list. As of writing:

- muse-spark-1.3 — latest model for coding and agentic workflows, with a 1,048,576-token context window, text/image/video/PDF input, tool calling, structured output, and search grounding.
- muse-spark-1.3-contributor — the same model with discounted pricing. Selecting this ID permits Meta to use your prompts and completions to train future models.
- muse-spark-1.1 — original Muse Spark model, still supported.

Both 1.3 IDs work with the Responses, Chat Completions, and Messages APIs. Meta notes that audio understanding in 1.3 is not fully supported and may produce degraded responses.

## Configuration
providers:
  - id: meta:muse-spark-1.3
    config:
      reasoning_effort: high
      max_completion_tokens: 8192
      temperature: 1.0

### Configuration Options

The provider accepts compatible OpenAI provider options. Notable behavior:

- reasoning_effort — minimal, low, medium, high, or xhigh. When omitted, the model picks its own reasoning depth. Muse Spark does not support none; the provider rejects it with a clear error. Reasoning tokens bill at the output rate and count toward the output cap.
- max_completion_tokens — caps generation on the chat endpoint (Meta accepts max_tokens only as a deprecated alias; if you set it, the provider forwards it as the canonical max_completion_tokens). On the Responses API the cap is max_output_tokens, and the provider maps max_completion_tokens/max_tokens onto it. When unset, no cap is sent so reasoning can use the full output budget.
- temperature — supported (0–2, API default 1.0). Promptfoo sends its deterministic default of 0 unless you override it.
- response_format — structured output with guaranteed JSON schema matching.
- tools / tool_choice — parallel tool calling with streamed arguments.
- prompt_cache_retention — in_memory or 24h for prompt caching; cached prompt tokens bill at the cached-input rate.
- seed — best-effort determinism.

On Chat Completions and Responses, promptfoo rejectslogprobs, n > 1, stop, and logit_bias before sending a request. It also rejects stream because these integrations expect a complete JSON response. OpenAI-scoped environment defaults (OPENAI_TEMPERATURE, OPENAI_TOP_P, OPENAI_MAX_COMPLETION_TOKENS, penalty variables) are not applied to Meta requests.

### Cost Tracking

Promptfoo computes token cost from Meta's published pricing, including the discounted rate for cached input:

Model | Input / 1M | Cached input / 1M | Output / 1M 
---|---|---|---
muse-spark-1.3, muse-spark-1.1 | $1.25 | $0.15 | $4.25 
muse-spark-1.3-contributor | $0.10 | $0.002 | $0.20 

Contributor pricing requires opting into Meta's training data terms by selecting the Contributor model ID. Override token prices withcost, inputCost, outputCost, or cacheReadCost (USD per token) for custom rates. Token cost excludes web-search charges.

## Responses API

meta:<model> (the default) and meta:responses:<model> target Meta's /v1/responses endpoint — the only Meta endpoint that carries reasoning across turns, with built-in web-search grounding:
providers:
  - id: meta:responses:muse-spark-1.3
    config:
      reasoning_effort: medium
      tools:
        - type: web_search

Withweb_search, the model grounds answers in real-time web results with inline citations. Web search bills separately ($2.50 per 1,000 queries) and is not included in promptfoo's computed token cost.

## Messages API

meta:messages:<model> targets Meta's Anthropic-compatible Messages endpoint (https://api.meta.ai/v1/messages) — the surface Anthropic-format coding agents such as Claude Code use. Use it to evaluate Muse Spark over the same wire format those agents send:
providers:
  - id: meta:messages:muse-spark-1.3
    config:
      max_tokens: 8192

The provider extends the Anthropic provider, so its options (max_tokens, tools, image and document content blocks, etc.) apply. It defaults max_tokens to 131,072 and enables streaming so the Anthropic SDK can safely handle long generations; streamed output is aggregated before grading. Authentication uses your Meta key as a bearer token (Authorization: Bearer), matching Meta's docs — Anthropic-scoped settings like ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, ANTHROPIC_MAX_TOKENS, ANTHROPIC_TEMPERATURE, custom headers, and Claude Code OAuth credentials are deliberately ignored on this surface.

Muse Spark's reasoning arrives on this surface as encryptedredacted_thinking blocks, so the provider defaults showThinking to false to keep the ciphertext out of graded output.

## Using with coding-agent providers

Meta positions Muse Spark as a backend for coding agents, and promptfoo's agentic providers can evaluate those setups end to end. In both recipes, setapiKey explicitly: the agent subprocesses inherit your shell environment, and an explicit key guarantees your Meta key is used instead of an ambient OPENAI_API_KEY or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY that belongs to another service.

### Codex CLI

Theopenai:codex-sdk provider drives Muse Spark over the Responses API:
providers:
  - id: openai:codex-sdk
    config:
      base_url: https://api.meta.ai/v1
      model: muse-spark-1.3
      apiKey: '{{env.MODEL_API_KEY}}'

The explicitapiKey is required — the provider does not read MODEL_API_KEY on its own, and without it an ambient OPENAI_API_KEY would be sent to the Meta endpoint instead.

### Claude Code

Theanthropic:claude-agent-sdk provider forwards config.env to the agent subprocess. Pass the environment Meta's guide prescribes, with apiKey set to your Meta key:
providers:
  - id: anthropic:claude-agent-sdk
    # Provider-level `env` outranks the eval's top-level `env`, pinning the
    # routing values a suite-wide ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL (e.g. an Anthropic
    # gateway) would otherwise override — which would send the Meta key there.
    env:
      ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL: https://api.meta.ai
      ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS: ''
    config:
      apiKey: '{{env.MODEL_API_KEY}}'
      env:
        ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL: https://api.meta.ai
        ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN: '{{env.MODEL_API_KEY}}'
        ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS: ''
        ANTHROPIC_MODEL: muse-spark-1.3
        ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL: muse-spark-1.3
        ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL: muse-spark-1.3
        ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL: muse-spark-1.3
        CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL: muse-spark-1.3
        ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH: 'true' # Claude Code disables MCP tool search for non-first-party hosts

warning

Do not omitapiKey, the empty ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS override, or the provider-level env block. The provider forwards its resolved API key into the agent subprocess as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY after env: is applied — if apiKey is unset and a real ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is exported in your shell, that Anthropic credential would be transmitted to Meta's endpoint. Clearing ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS prevents an inherited gateway or proxy secret from being sent to Meta. The provider-level env block matters because the subprocess environment is layered process.env < config.env < provider/suite env: without the pin, a top-level env.ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL in the same config would silently re-route the agent — and your Meta key — to that URL.

Pin every model alias as shown — Claude Code otherwise routes background tasks, Plan Mode, or subagents to Claude models the Meta API doesn't serve. See Meta's coding agents guide for the full setup pattern.

## Example Usage
providers:
  - id: meta:muse-spark-1.3
  - id: openai:gpt-5.5

prompts:
  - 'Summarize the following in one sentence: {{text}}'

tests:
  - vars:
      text: 'Promptfoo is an open-source tool for testing and evaluating LLM apps.'

Get started with a runnable example:
npx promptfoo@latest init --example provider-meta

## API Details

- Base URL:https://api.meta.ai/v1 (override with apiBaseUrl; the Messages surface uses the bare host https://api.meta.ai).
- OpenAI-compatible chat completions (/chat/completions) and Responses (/responses) endpoints, plus the Anthropic-compatible Messages (/messages) endpoint.
- Rate limits apply per team, not per key: 3,000 RPM / 4M TPM for Standard models and 100 RPM / 3M TPM for Contributor models.
- Full API documentation.

# Llama-3.1

## 1. Model Introduction
Llama 3.1 is a collection of pretrained and instruction tuned generative models, released in July 2024 by Meta. These models are available in 8B, 70B and 405B sizes, with the 405B variant being the most capable fully-open source model at the time. These models bring open intelligence to all, with several new features and improvements:
- Stronger General Intelligence: These models showcase significant improvements in coding, state-of-the-art tool use, and overall stronger reasoning capabilities.
- Extended Context Length: Llama 3.1 extends the context length to 128K tokens to improve performance over long context tasks such as summarization and code reasoning.
- Tool Use: Llama 3.1 is trained to interact with a search engine, python interpreter and mathematical engine, and also improves zero-shot tool use capabilities to interact with potentially unseen tools.
- Multilinguality: Llama 3.1 supports 7 languages in addition to English: French, German, Hindi, Italian, Portuguese, Spanish, and Thai.

## 2. SGLang Installation
SGLang offers multiple installation methods. You can choose the most suitable installation method based on your hardware platform and requirements. Please refer to the official SGLang installation guide for installation instructions.

## 3. Model Deployment
This section provides deployment configurations optimized for different hardware platforms including NVIDIA GPUs, AMD GPUs, Intel Arc Pro B-Series GPUs(codename: BMG (Battlemage)), and Intel Xeon CPUs.

### 3.1 Basic Configuration
Interactive Command Generator: Use the configuration selector below to generate a launch command for Llama 3.1 collection of models.
Hardware Platform

Model Size

Category

Quantization

Tool Call Parser

Optimization Mode

Run this Command:

  --model-path meta-llama/Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct \
  --tp 2

### 3.2 Configuration Tips
Speculative Decoding (NVIDIA GPUs):
- Using Speculative Decoding for latency-sensitive scenarios:
- --speculative-algorithm EAGLE3: Speculative decoding algorithm
- --speculative-num-steps 3: Number of speculative verification rounds
- --speculative-eagle-topk 1: Top-k sampling for draft tokens
- --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4: Number of draft tokens per step
- --speculative-draft-model-path: The path of the draft model weights. This can be a local folder or a Hugging Face repo ID such as yuhuili/EAGLE3-LLaMA3.1-Instruct-8B.

- Hardware-Aware TP: MI355X (256GB memory) supports lower TP values compared to MI300X/MI325X (192GB)
- Verified TP Configurations:
- MI300X/MI325X: 405B BF16 (TP=8), 405B FP8 (TP=4), 70B/8B (TP=1)
- MI355X: 405B BF16 (TP=4), 405B FP8 (TP=2), 70B/8B (TP=1)

- FP8 Model Variants:
- 405B: Use Meta’s officialmeta-llama/Llama-3.1-405B-Instruct-FP8
- 70B/8B: Use AMD’s optimizedamd/Llama-3.1-{size}-Instruct-FP8-KV

- 405B: Use Meta’s official
- Tool Calling: Enable with--tool-call-parser llama3 for Instruct models

- Please refer to theNotes part in the serving engine launching section in the SGLang CPU server document to better understand how to configure the arguments, especially for TP (tensor parallel) and NUMA binding settings.

## 4. Model Invocation

### 4.1 Basic Usage
SGLang exposes an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. First, start the server
Command
sglang serve \
  --model-path  Meta-Llama/Llama-3.1-405B-Instruct \
  --tp 8

Output Example:

Example

    base_url="http://localhost:8000/v1",
    api_key="EMPTY",
)

resp = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="Meta-Llama/Llama-3.1-405B-Instruct",
    messages=[
        {"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful coding assistant."},

Output
**Exponential Backoff Retry Function in Python**
=====================================================

Below is a Python function that uses the `requests` library to retry a request with exponential backoff.

```python
import requests
import time
import random

def exponential_backoff_retry(url, method, retries=3, backoff_factor=1, max_delay=60):
    """
    Retry a request with exponential backoff.

    Args:
        url (str): The URL to make the request to.
        method (str): The HTTP method to use (e.g. 'GET', 'POST', etc.).
        retries (int): The number of retries to attempt. Defaults to 3.
        backoff_factor (int): The factor to multiply the delay by for each retry. Defaults to 1.
        max_delay (int): The maximum delay to wait between retries in seconds. Defaults to 60.

    Returns:
        The response object from the successful request.
    """

    delay = 1
    for attempt in range(retries + 1):
        try:
            response = requests.request(method, url)
            response.raise_for_status()  # Raise an exception for HTTP errors
            return response
        except requests.RequestException as e:
            if attempt < retries:
                # Calculate the delay for this retry
                delay = min(delay * backoff_factor, max_delay)
                # Add a random jitter to the delay to prevent thundering herd problem
                delay += random.uniform(0, delay * 0.1)
                # Wait for the calculated delay before retrying
                time.sleep(delay)
            else:
                # If all retries have failed, raise the exception
                raise e
...

#### 4.2.1 Tool Calling

# Print accumulated tool calls

# Llama-3.3-70B

## 1. Model Introduction
Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct is Meta’s latest 70 billion parameter instruction-tuned language model, featuring improved performance and efficiency over Llama 3.1. With a 128K token context window and enhanced capabilities across reasoning, coding, and multilingual tasks, Llama 3.3 delivers state-of-the-art results while maintaining accessibility for production deployment. Key Features:
- Enhanced Performance: Improved instruction following, reasoning, and task completion over Llama 3.1
- Tool Calling: Native support for function calling and tool use scenarios
- Multilingual Support: Optimized for 8 languages (English, German, French, Italian, Portuguese, Hindi, Spanish, and Thai)
- Extended Context: 128K token context window for processing long documents and complex tasks
- Efficient Deployment: 70B parameters enable deployment on single GPU with AMD MI300X

## 2. SGLang Installation
Please refer to the official SGLang installation guide for installation instructions.

## 3. Model Deployment

# Meta AI战略报告（附发展趋势、竞争格局与市场空间）
