cross_cutting.content:
# From several months to one week: How Zhiyue Chuangda ZAI accelerates enterprise AI deployment

氪友LvEz2026-10-22 16:48

Zhiyue Chuangda launches the ZAI platform to shorten enterprises' AI development cycle and deploy multiple product lines.

Wuhan Zhiyue Chuangda Technology adopts the dual-engine architecture of "Intelligent Central Base + AI Development Framework", which shortens the delivery cycle of enterprise customized AI systems from several months to one week. At present, its products have expanded from the development platform to desktop terminals, all-in-one machines and C-end scientific research applications.

In July 2025, Wuhan Zhiyue Chuangda Technology Co., Ltd. launched ZAI (Zero to AI), an enterprise-level one-stop AI agent development platform. According to the team, enterprises can complete the development and launch of business intelligence based on this platform in as fast as only one week.

Tang Shengwu, founder of Zhiyue Chuangda, has 15 years of experience in the IT industry, and has served as architect, technical director, senior engineer and other positions. The core team is composed of a number of technical experts from well-known technology enterprises. The project started technical R&D in January 2025. The team spent half a year polishing the first version and continued to iterate afterwards. At present, it has completed the layout on four product lines: B-end platform, desktop office, software-hardware integration and C-end scientific research assistant.

## I. Three Thresholds for Enterprise AI Implementation: Technology, Cost and Security

The capabilities of large models have been rapidly popularized in the past three years, but on the enterprise side, there is still a considerable gap between "being able to use AI" and "using AI well". The founder of the team summarized the common difficulties faced by enterprises into three points: First, the technical threshold is high. An available agent involves multiple links such as model invocation, knowledge base construction, tool orchestration, permission and security. It is difficult for enterprises without AI engineering experience to connect these links on their own. Second, the implementation cycle is long. The traditional customized development from demand sorting to system launch is often calculated in months, which cannot meet the timeliness requirement of business. Third, it is difficult to balance cost and security. Building a self-owned team requires large investment, while standardized SaaS products are difficult to match the personalized business processes and private data requirements of enterprises.

As a result, many enterprises' AI attempts remain at the single-point pilot stage and are difficult to enter the core business process. "Either spend a lot of money on self-development, or make do with general products". This mismatch is exactly the market gap targeted by Zhiyue Chuangda's ZAI platform.

## II. Dual-engine Architecture: Shortening Agent Development to Minute Level

The technical core of ZAI is the dual-engine architecture composed of the self-developed ZAI intelligent central base and the EasyAI development framework, which solve the two problems of "standardized access" and "personalized customization" respectively.

The base is responsible for compatibility and openness: the platform supports access to mainstream large language models such as DeepSeek, Tongyi Qianwen, ERNIE, covers multiple types of structured and unstructured data sources, is compatible with Skills extensions of Agents such as OpenClaw and WorkBuddy, and supports enterprise self-defined Skills development. The development framework is responsible for efficiency: through flexible configuration, standardized components and preset scenario templates, developers can quickly combine models, data and tools without repeatedly building underlying capabilities, complete customers' personalized business customization, shorten the delivery cycle from week level to day level, and realize agile iteration and rapid implementation.

In terms of delivery form, Zhiyue Chuangda ZAI supports private deployment and all-in-one machine delivery, and provides capabilities including resource isolation, permission management, auditing, monitoring and log analysis, so as to meet the compliance requirements of enterprises for data not leaving the internal network. The platform also has a built-in agent store, covering common scenarios such as general office and document processing. Enterprises can either deploy with one click or carry out in-depth customization on this basis.

## III. Platform Authorization + Customized Service: Prioritizing Knowledge-intensive Industries

In terms of target users, Zhiyue Chuangda ZAI mainly targets medium and large enterprises with clear business processes but lacking AI engineering capabilities, especially knowledge-intensive industries such as medicine, law and intellectual property, consulting, and education. The common characteristics of these scenarios are a large number of unstructured documents, strong dependence on expert experience, and high sensitivity to data security.

At present, Zhiyue Chuangda ZAI has been implemented and verified in the fields of pharmaceutical R&D, enterprise consulting, education enrollment, intellectual property and other fields. According to the team, an intellectual property company built an AI patent agent based on ZAI to automate tedious document work such as auxiliary processing of disclosure documents and specification generation. According to its internal statistics, the overall efficiency has increased by more than 30%. A pharmaceutical R&D enterprise used it to build a vertical R&D knowledge base, realizing intelligent retrieval of massive literatures and experimental data, and shortening the R&D cycle. A person in charge of an enterprise consulting customer feedbacked: "In the past, it was difficult to precipitate expert experience, and the quality of new employees' consultation was uneven. After using the exclusive knowledge base agent created by Zhiyue Chuangda ZAI, we not only realized the digital reuse of experience, but also greatly improved the speed of scheme generation and report quality, with the cost much lower than self-development."

In terms of business model, Zhiyue Chuangda adopts the combination of "platform authorization + customized service": enterprises pay the platform authorization fee at one time. According to the team, this price is far lower than the investment of enterprises in building similar systems by themselves. The team also provides services including AI implementation scheme design, project implementation assistance and after-sales upgrade, which takes into account the scale effect of standardized delivery and the unit price space of personalized customization.

## IV. Formed Product Matrix: From Development Platform to Software-hardware Integration

From the first version in July 2025 to now, Zhiyue Chuangda ZAI has gone beyond the stage of "single development platform". In March 2026, ZAI 2.0 with full autonomous planning capability was launched. The agent no longer only executes according to the preset process, but can independently disassemble tasks, plan execution steps, select and call tools. The work on the enterprise side has changed from "building process" to "giving goals". In May 2026, ZAI Work for desktop office scenarios was released, covering document processing, knowledge Q&A and process automation. In the same period, Zhiyue Chuangda cooperated with hardware manufacturers to launch the ZAI agent all-in-one machine, which encapsulates the model, platform and computing power into one device, so that enterprises can access it immediately after unboxing. In August 2026, the C-end scientific research agent platform for scientific research scenarios was launched, extending the product line from B-end to C-end.

These product lines share the same set of base: ZAI Work is embedded in the daily office desktop of employees, the all-in-one machine meets the demand of data not leaving the internal network and ready-to-use, and the C-end scientific research platform is the extension of these capabilities in professional personal scenarios. For customers, the same agent can be built on the platform, called on the desktop, and run privately in the all-in-one machine. The choice of delivery form no longer comes at the cost of capability sacrifice, which is also the basis for the standardization of platform authorization fees and the on-demand pricing of customized services.

According to the team's plan, the team will expand its staff to improve delivery capacity in 2026; complete scale verification in 2027, expand B-end customers and establish channel cooperation to improve delivery efficiency and customer unit price; explore overseas expansion in 2028, export standardized SaaS and industry solutions to realize diversified revenue structure, and strive to serve more than 1000 enterprise customers by 2030.

The founder of the team said, "We technical people believe that intelligence is the underlying driving force for progress. We are not doing this project to ride the AI trend. After more than ten years of experience in the industry, we are very clear about the real pain points of enterprise transformation. Technical parameters are cold, but the pain points of B-end business are warm. We hope to transform our accumulated engineering implementation capabilities into AI tools that enterprises can afford and use well."

According to forecasts from third-party institutions such as iiMedia Research, the market size of China's enterprise-level AI agent market is expected to exceed 30 billion yuan in 2026. With the continuous release of demand for enterprise intelligent transformation, this track is still expanding rapidly, and the key to competition is shifting from model capability to engineering delivery capability.

cross_cutting.title: Sia launches AgentLaunch to put AI agent building in the hands of business teams
cross_cutting.description: Sia launches AgentLaunch to put AI agent building in the hands of business teams ... a 10-week programme that teaches business employees to design, build, and deploy their own AI agents, with Sia engineers and central governance in place for the more complex use cases.
cross_cutting.content:
# Sia launches AgentLaunch to put AI agent building in the hands of business teams

Global consultancy Sia has launched AgentLaunch, a 10-week programme that teaches business employees to design, build, and deploy their own AI agents, with Sia engineers and central governance in place for the more complex use cases.

The launch comes as many organizations move beyond experimenting with generative AI and confront a different challenge: how to scale it.

“AgentLaunch is built for them,” says Carlos Guevara, partner at Sia and lead of the initiative in the Middle East. “Participants keep their normal jobs, spend a few hours each week bringing real business problems into the program, and finish with a Demo Day where they present working agents to the people who can approve them. The aim is to leave clients with both working agents and staff who can build more.

According to Guevara, AgentLaunch plays into one of the main challenges around AI deployment: “It’s increasingly one of capacity rather than ideas.” Treating AI as another monolithic corporate technology project, he emphasizes, fundamentally misunderstands both the scale of the opportunity and the economics of execution.

“Most organizations do not have a shortage of AI ideas anymore,” Guevara says. “If you ask employees where AI could improve their daily work, you very quickly end up with hundreds or even thousands of potential use cases. A central AI team will never be able to build all of those.”

Instead of centralizing every workflow within an overburdened technical team, AgentLaunch is based on a hybrid model: central technology teams provide the platforms, governance, security and specialist engineering, while business users are enabled to develop many of the agents closest to their own work.

The objective is not to bypass IT, Guevara stresses, but to prevent central development teams from becoming the bottleneck for every AI opportunity in the organization.

## Moving AI development closer to the problem

The core philosophy of AgentLaunch rests on breaking the traditional backlog that forms when corporate technology units attempt to design every single workflow. But the argument for ademocratizing agent development is not only about development capacity. It is also about knowledge.

Guevara highlights how ‘domain mastery’ is often trapped at the operational level rather than within technical teams. A procurement specialist understands which contractual exception is genuinely important. An operations manager knows where a process really breaks down. An HR professional understands the context behind a workforce decision. Much of that knowledge is tacit and can be difficult to capture in a traditional requirements document.

“The person doing the job usually understands the problem better than anybody else,” Guevara says.

Bringing the person who understands the problem closer to the development process can therefore shorten the cycle between identifying an opportunity, building a solution, testing it and improving it. Sometimes they become the same person. The result, Guevara says, is that it “dramatically accelerates the learning cycle.”

It can also change the cultural dynamic around AI. Instead of AI being something designed centrally and deployed to employees, business teams become active participants in redesigning their own work.

Carlos Guevara is partner at Sia in the Middle East

## The Excel analogy, with an important difference

A useful way to think about Agentic AI is to look at what happened when spreadsheets became widely available across organisations. Excel effectively democratised access to computing power for business users. Suddenly, people across Finance, Operations, Commercial, HR and other functions could create their own spreadsheets. The adoption was largely organic and business-led.

Most users built relatively simple spreadsheets. Some became advanced users and created highly sophisticated models, automations and macros. Nobody would have thought: “I need a spreadsheet – I should call IT and ask them to build it for me.”

“IT provided the technology and the environment. Business users created the applications. That is the shift we are now beginning to see with Agentic AI,” says Guevara.

The objective is not that every employee becomes an AI engineer. It is that business users increasingly have the ability to build many of the agents they need themselves – because they understand the problem, the workflow and the context better than anyone else. “Just as Excel moved spreadsheet creation into the hands of the business, Agentic AI has the potential to move a large part of AI solution creation there too.”

## Building champions across a 10-week accelerator program

AgentLaunch is typically delivered over 10 weeks on a part-time basis. Participants remain in their normal roles and dedicate several hours each week to the program.

Rather than working through hypothetical training exercises, they bring actual business problems from their departments and progressively turn them into working agents. Sia combines training with hands-on coaching, while working with the client’s technology teams to establish the platform, governance and guardrails around development.

Importantly, participants are also taught to assess the economics of what they are building. They learn how to define expected benefits, establish measures for value realization and develop a business case that can support an implementation or scale-up decision. The program concludes with a Demo Day, where participants demonstrate their solutions to relevant business and technology stakeholders.

“The objective of the programme is twofold: producing working AI solutions and creating a group of employees capable of identifying and developing the next generation of opportunities. The client finishes with both working solutions and empowered internal AI champions,” Guevara says.

## Managing AI consumption

Continuing his Excel analogy, Guevara notes that there is one important area where the comparison breaks down. While desktop productivity software incurred modest incremental operating costs once a license was acquired, AI services involve dynamic computing consumption that demands strict enterprise governance.

“AI brings a consumption economy. Every interaction consumes tokens and computing resources, and once agents operate at scale, inefficient design can generate significant cost. So AI consumption needs to be monitored centrally – almost like a FinOps discipline for AI,” Guevara adds. “The AI center of excellence should have visibility over which agents are consuming what, which models they use, and where optimization is possible.”

“That is why AgentLaunch teaches participants to think not only about building agents, but about building economically viable agents,” he adds.

Sia’s approach builds that economic discipline into the business case phase, exploring total cost determinants including development, infrastructure, model and token consumption, maintenance, and governance. “These factors have to be weighed against the value an agentic AI solution is expected to deliver through productivity, quality, risk reduction, revenue, or cost savings.”

## From individual agents to organizational capability

Recognised as an AI pioneer in the global consulting landscape, Sia has to date already developed an ecosystem of more than 1,000 agents across functions and industries. “We have rolled out dozens of these agentic solutions in the Middle East too, including in the government and energy sectors,” Guevara says.

“For example, we have an agentic solution that helps government organisations identify service pain points and reimagine optimised journeys for their customers. This solution was built collaboratively with the inputs of service designers and owners from across 12 entities. The result is impressive: it helps reduce the service design process from weeks to minutes.”

These are the kinds of use cases driving growing demand for agentic AI among organisations and individuals. “Six or twelve months ago, many organisations were asking, what can AI do for me? Today the question is increasingly: How do we scale it across the organization? That is exactly the problem AgentLaunch is designed to address.”

Guevara applies the same thinking to his own work. “I increasingly use agents as a portfolio of digital capabilities around my work,” he says, relying on them for research, meeting preparation, analysing information, challenging ideas, developing proposals, and accelerating content creation.

The longer-term implication could extend well beyond individual productivity tools. “Today we still talk about ‘using an AI agent’ as though it is something unusual,” he says. “I think fairly soon we will simply think about teams composed of human and digital capabilities.”

For managers, he argues, that could introduce a new management question: “what should I do myself, what should my team do, and what should I delegate to an agent?”

At Sia, they’ve embraced this philosophy at the outset. “AgentLaunch is one of our offerings designed to help organizations start answering that question at scale, not simply by giving them more AI solutions, but by developing the people capable of building the next ones.”

# Vultr and AMD Expand Global Collaboration with New AI Infrastructure in India

- October 22, 2026 06:17 GMT+700

New Chennai deployment will create one of the world’s largest AMD Instinct™ superclusters, expanding AI compute access in India

Chennai, India--(ANTARA/Business Wire)--Vultr, the world’s largest privately-held cloud infrastructure company, today announced a major expansion of its AMD powered infrastructure for enterprise and sovereign cloud initiatives. Vultr will deploy AMD Instinct™ MI355X GPUs in a new 20 MW supercluster in Chennai, India, creating the country’s largest AMD Instinct deployment and giving Vultr two of the world’s largest AMD AI infrastructure deployments globally, alongside its flagship supercluster in Springfield, Ohio. With 288GB of HBM3E memory and 8TB/s of memory bandwidth per GPU, AMD Instinct MI355X GPUs provide the performance and memory capacity required to develop and deploy increasingly complex AI models at scale.

The Chennai supercluster is designed to serve AI labs and foundation model builders, AI-native startups, enterprises, and research and academic institutions. It will support demanding AI workloads including large language model and foundation model training, fine-tuning and high-throughput inference, providing the compute capacity organizations need to develop and deploy AI at scale.

“Enterprises deploying AI at scale need infrastructure they can access locally to meet data sovereignty, data residency, and latency requirements,” said J.J. Kardwell, CEO of Vultr. “Vultr’s Chennai supercluster, powered by AMD MI355X GPUs, gives organizations in India the capacity to train, fine-tune, and run inference on in-country infrastructure.”

Vultr’s longstanding relationship with AMD spans the AMD Instinct GPU roadmap, from MI300X and MI325X to MI355X and the planned MI455X and AMD Helios rack-scale architecture, together with the AMD EPYC data center CPUs that power Vultr VX1 Cloud Compute. The Chennai deployment extends that collaboration as AMD and Vultr expand access to advanced AI infrastructure through Vultr’s global cloud footprint. Looking ahead, Vultr plans significant additional capacity expansion in 2027, including AMD Instinct™ MI455X GPUs and the AMD Helios™ rack-scale AI architecture, broadening global access to next-generation AI infrastructure.

The Chennai supercluster will also leverage the AMD ROCm™ open software ecosystem, giving developers access to widely used AI frameworks, libraries and models, with greater flexibility and choice in how they develop and deploy AI workloads. The open software approach also supports AI innovation in India through open-source software and community-driven development.

“India has the talent and ideas to build the next generation of AI. Access to compute at this scale will help turn more of those ideas into reality,” said Jaya Jagadish, Country Head & SVP Engineering, AMD India. “Through our collaboration with Vultr, we’re expanding access to AMD Instinct compute in India, backed by the AMD ROCm open software ecosystem, giving researchers, startups and enterprises greater choice and flexibility in how they develop and deploy AI.”

The launch comes as demand for sovereign cloud infrastructure is rising globally. Security concerns, regulatory requirements and performance expectations are intensifying the need for in-country infrastructure that can support advanced AI workloads. With 34 global cloud data center regions, Vultr provides secure, compliant infrastructure at a predictable cost to enterprises, AI innovators, and government agencies in 17 countries across six continents. The Chennai deployment reflects a broader shift toward geographically-distributed AI infrastructure, bringing large-scale compute closer to where data is created and AI applications are deployed.

To learn more about Vultr’s collaboration with AMD, visit www.vultr.com/cloudalliance/amd/ or contact sales to get started.

About Vultr

Vultr is on a mission to make high-performance cloud infrastructure easy to use, affordable, and locally accessible for enterprises and AI innovators around the world. Vultr is trusted by hundreds of thousands of active customers across 185 countries for its flexible, scalable, global Cloud Compute, Cloud GPU, Bare Metal, and Cloud Storage solutions. In December 2024 Vultr announced an equity financing at a $3.5 billion valuation. Founded by David Aninowsky and self-funded for over a decade, Vultr has grown to become the world’s largest privately-held cloud infrastructure company.

# Armada, Johnson Controls plan 500MW AI infrastructure rollout

#### Author: Joe Peck

Armada, a US provider of modular edge data centres and connectivity for remote sites, plans to work with Johnson Controls, a global provider of smart building technologies, to build 500MW of distributed sovereign super intelligence (SI) infrastructure in 2027, using factory-integrated systems based on NVIDIA’s DSX POD reference design and Vera Rubin platform.

Announced at NVIDIA GTC, the collaboration will combine engineering, manufacturing, and deployment to deliver modular infrastructure with cabling, wiring, piping, and functional validation completed before shipment.

## Factory-built infrastructure aims to accelerate deployment

The NVIDIA DSX POD reference design moves repeatable construction work from data centre sites into factories. Compute, networking, rack-level power, plumbing for liquid cooling, and supporting infrastructure are integrated and validated before delivery.

On site, the containers are connected to prepared power, water, cooling, and networking infrastructure, with capacity expanded by adding standardised units.

Armada will use NVIDIA DSX Air to simulate AI factories and validate its Bridge GPU management software before shipment. Once deployed, NVIDIA DSX MaxLPS will help manage power and workloads to maximise computing throughput within each site’s available power capacity.

Dan Wright, co-founder and CEO of Armada, says, “The SI race isn’t going to be won by whoever pours concrete the fastest. Companies and nations can have the chips, the land, the power, and the ambition and still be told to wait years for a building.

“The NVIDIA DSX POD reference design lets us cut that wait out of the equation. We build the SI factory in one of our Galleon Forge factories, ship it, connect it, and our customers are generating tokens in months on infrastructure they own and control.”

## Distributed capacity for sovereign AI

Armada says conventional 50MW facilities can take years to become IT-ready and require around 600,000 on-site labour hours. It also cites a projected construction workforce shortfall of 288,000 workers by 2027 as a challenge to expanding capacity.

The company plans to deploy modular SI facilities close to energy sources, including stranded, renewable, and off-peak power. Its proposed architecture is designed to operate without cloud dependencies, allowing customers to retain control of their models, data, and infrastructure.

Charlie Boyle, Vice President of DGX Systems at NVIDIA, notes, “The demand for compute is outpacing the speed at which the world can build the facilities to house it.

“By utilising the NVIDIA DSX POD reference design, Armada can deliver factory-built, Vera Rubin-based containers to customers. Together with Johnson Controls, Armada is positioned to bring Vera Rubin-based factories to customers who need capacity now, wherever their energy and data are.”

## Manufacturing partnership

Armada brings experience deploying modular data centre infrastructure in remote and challenging environments, including Alaska, a US Navy littoral combat ship, and desert locations in the Middle East.

The company says its manufacturing and deployment capabilities will support the planned rollout, with Johnson Controls contributing thermal management technology, engineering, and global manufacturing capacity.

Joakim Weidemanis, CEO of Johnson Controls, comments, “NVIDIA is rapidly advancing the age of intelligence and reshaping the infrastructure required to support it.

“Our collaboration with Armada combines their expertise in deploying compute at the edge with Johnson Controls’ advanced thermal management technology, engineering capabilities, and global manufacturing scale. This combination delivers high-performance infrastructure engineered to quickly bring capacity online where and when it’s needed.”

Under the collaboration, NVIDIA will design, test, and validate the DSX POD reference design for the Vera Rubin platform, whilst Armada will engineer, manufacture, integrate, customise, service, and deliver the modular data centres.

cross_cutting.title: Nvidia plans sovereign AI factories with European telecom operators

Finnish telecom Elisa conducted Europe's first field trial of AI-RAN with Nvidia over 5G.
cross_cutting.content:
# Nvidia plans sovereign AI factories with European telecom operators

Nvidia is collaborating with European telecom operators to set up AI factories that enhance local infrastructure. Around ten telecom companies in EMEA are set to adopt Nvidia's advanced computing hardware for various AI applications. Deutsche Telekom plans to expand its industrial AI cloud platform using Nvidia's technology for physical applications. Elisa has successfully conducted a pioneering AI-RAN trial integrating multiple services on Nvidia's platform.

Nvidia plans to help European telecom operators establish sovereign AI factories, marking an expansion into the telecom sector, SDxCentral reported on Wednesday.

The company confirmed at its GTC event in Berlin that approximately 10 telecom operators in EMEA have committed to using its accelerated computing hardware. This hardware will power various applications, including industrial AI clouds and AI-RAN.

Ian Buck, Nvidia's VP and GM for hyperscale and high-performance computing, stated in a press briefing that this represents a "new path to market." This path aims to expand AI infrastructure and services across Europe.

Nvidia has already invested $1 billion in Nokia. Companies like Deutsche Telekom, BT, and Orange have trialed GPU-accelerated platforms or hosted Nemotron open models. This aims to unlock new business models through AI.

Buck noted that telecom companies own about 20 per cent of Europe's data centres. This number rises to over 1,500 when including edge sites.

Nvidia argues that telecom operators are well-suited to support sovereign infrastructure. They already own data centres, regional sites, and cell sites with power, fibre, and spectrum.

Deutsche Telekom plans to expand its Nvidia-powered industrial AI cloud platform. This platform hosts open models for physical AI applications such as robotics. The carrier is utilising Nvidia's Arc server lines, including the Blackwell-based RTX Pro 6000, for inference between devices and the network edge.

Orange has introduced new voice intelligence services for enterprises and emergency responders. Finnish telecom Elisa conducted Europe's first field trial of AI-RAN with Nvidia over 5G. This trial ran voice, mobile data, and vision AI on a single accelerated computing platform.

Deutsche Telekom CEO Tim Höttges commented on integrating AI where it makes a real difference. He highlighted bringing intelligence closer to high-tech industries. Höttges added that companies perform best with optimal networks and smart AI. He said that together with Nvidia, they are making this happen.

cross_cutting.title: SoftBank, Nokia target 2027 for commercial AI-RAN trial in Japan
cross_cutting.description: In a trial planned for 2027, SoftBank and Nokia aim to move AI-RAN out of laboratory environments and validate its performance under real-world, commercial traffic conditions. ... Nokia and SoftBank have agreed to conduct a commercial AI-RAN (AI-Radio Access Network) field trial in Japan in 2027.
cross_cutting.content:
# SoftBank, Nokia target 2027 for commercial AI-RAN trial in Japan

In a trial planned for 2027, SoftBank and Nokia aim to move AI-RAN out of laboratory environments and validate its performance under real-world, commercial traffic conditions.

Gigi Onag,Senior Editor, APAC,Light Reading

October 22, 2026

3 Min Read

(Source: SOPA Images Limited/Alamy Stock Photo)

Nokia and SoftBank have agreed to conduct a commercial AI-RAN (AI-Radio Access Network) field trial in Japan in 2027. This marks a notable step forward since the trial will take place in a genuine commercial network environment under real commercial traffic conditions, rather than in a controlled lab or isolated testbed setting.

The trial aims to assess the feasibility of running AI and radio network workloads on shared computing infrastructure simultaneously. The two companies essentially want to determine whether the same physical infrastructure used to handle network traffic could also be used to process AI computing tasks, which could improve overall resource utilization and efficiency.

The trial will see Nokia’s AI-native anyRAN Cloud RAN software combined with SoftBank’s AITRAS core AI-RAN platform. The trial will also heavily rely on Nvidia’s Aerial RAN Computer (ARC) platform. The underlying hardware architecture features Nvidia Grace CPUs, Nvidia RTX PRO 4500 GPUs and Nvidia ConnectX-8 networking cards, which can handle heavy AI and radio workloads simultaneously on a single, shared computing infrastructure.

The management of radio and AI resources will be coordinated by integrating the Nokia MantaRay management platform with the AITRAS Orchestrator.

According to SoftBank, not only are telecom networks increasingly required to accommodate growing data traffic, they are also required to provide the computing capabilities needed for low-latency, real-time AI processing as generative AI, AI agents, and physical AI continue to evolve.

The Japanese operator is developing the AITRAS Orchestrator, a platform designed to run AI and RAN workloads on shared infrastructure. In real time, it will monitor demand for computing resources used for AI processing and RAN control, allocating resources flexibly and dynamically based on factors such as resource availability, application requirements and projected power consumption.

SoftBank said that the field trial will assess the suitability of AITRAS as a common platform for hosting RAN software and AI applications from multiple vendors, without the limitations imposed by a specific RAN software implementation.

"Our field trial with Nokia will mark a significant milestone in moving AI-RAN from concept toward commercialization," Ryuji Wakikawa, SoftBank Corp. senior vice president and CTO, said in a statement. "We will further advance AI-RAN validation toward commercialization and work toward a new era of networks that deliver both connectivity and AI services."

##### Transition toward AI-native network architecture

In a separate statement, Nokia said that its latest agreement with SoftBank builds on their ongoing collaboration in AI-RAN, which is supported by Nvidia’s accelerated computing node.

The Finnish equipment vendor added that the trial will contribute to the wider industry shift toward AI-native network architectures by exploring how operators can introduce new capabilities more quickly and support the development of new AI applications at the network edge.

The trial will explore how AI-RAN could support richer, AI-driven experiences, lower-latency services, and new applications powered by real-time intelligence. Future use cases could include physical AI, immersive digital experiences, robotics and autonomous systems that require close interaction between AI and connectivity.

Pallavi Mahajan, Nokia's chief technology and AI officer, noted that their ongoing collaboration with SoftBank is a stepping stone toward developing the automated, AI-native network architectures required for future 6G networks.

"By bringing AI and RAN workloads onto common, programmable infrastructure, AI-RAN has the potential to unlock new levels of spectral efficiency while providing the distributed intelligence needed to support physical AI," she said. "As the boundaries between network and compute continue to blur, this distributed infrastructure can become a powerful platform for both connectivity and AI."

## About the Author

Senior Editor, APAC, Light Reading

Gigi Onag is Senior Editor, APAC, Light Reading. She has been a technology journalist for more than 15 years, covering various aspects of enterprise IT across Asia-Pacific.

She started with regional IT publications under CMP Asia (now Informa), including Asia Computer Weekly, Intelligent Enterprise Asia and Network Computing Asia and Teledotcom Asia. This was followed by stints with Computerworld Hong Kong and sister publications FutureIoT and FutureCIO. She had contributed articles to South China Morning Post, TechTarget and PC Market among others.

She interspersed her career as a technology editor with a brief sojourn into public relations before returning to journalism, joining the editorial team of Mix Magazine, a MICE publication and its sister publication Business Traveller Asia Pacific.

Gigi is based in Hong Kong and is keen to delve deeper into the region’s wide wild world of telecoms.

cross_cutting.title: KDDI Collaborates with Broadcom on Network Infrastructure Technology for the Social Implementation of AI | KDDI Newsroom
cross_cutting.description: TOKYO, Japan―October 22, 2026―KDDI Corporation today announced a technical partnership with Broadcom Inc. ... the two companies will collaborate to archive optical-electronic convergence (Note 1) for inter-GPU networks, aiming to reduce power consumption in AI data centers.
cross_cutting.content:
## ―Advancing the communications infrastructure from data centers to homes to support AI applications―

KDDI Corporation

TOKYO, Japan―October 22, 2026―KDDI Corporation today announced a technical partnership with Broadcom Inc. (Headquarters: Palo Alto, California; President and CEO: Hock E. Tan; hereinafter "Broadcom") on network infrastructure technology to advance the social implementation of AI.
Under this partnership, the two companies will collaborate to archive optical-electronic convergence (Note 1) for inter-GPU networks, aiming to reduce power consumption in AI data centers. Starting today, they will begin a joint verification ("this verification") of Co-Packaged Optics (Note 2) ("CPO") technology. Based on the results of this verification, the companies aim to establish a network architecture that realizes optical-electronic convergence within KDDI's AI data centers.

Furthermore, for in-home broadband services -the final link to our customers- the companies will explore migrating to next-generation FTTH by leveraging Broadcom's expertise in opto-electric conversion technology. By holistically advancing the communication environment from data centers to homes, KDDI aims to create an environment where customers can seamlessly use AI services to generate new AI-powered experiences.

### ■Background

- With the recent spread of AI, the importance of the communications infrastructure that supports everything from training and inference in AI data centers to AI services used in the home has been increasing. For the further social implementation of AI, it is crucial to have both a high-speed, low-power communication foundation within data centers and a high-bandwidth, low-latency network connecting data centers to homes.
- Broadcom possesses semiconductor and network technologies for AI data centers and communication equipment.
- KDDI possesses technology and expertise cultivated through the construction and operation of communication networks and data centers. In an AI-driven society, KDDI is promoting the realization of its "Digital Belt," which combines assets like data centers and submarine cables with technologies like APN and 6G to build a nationwide low-latency network and AI computing resource infrastructure covering land, sea, and air.

### ■About this Verification

The two companies will work on reducing the power consumption of networks using CPO technology to achieve optical-electronic convergence for inter-GPU networks in AI data centers.
In this verification, KDDI will build a test environment in its AI data center and introduce a CPO switch equipped with modules of Broadcom's latest generation Ethernet switching chip, "Tomahawk 6" (Note 3), and optical engines "Davisson" (Note 4). In addition to verifying the power reduction benefits of the CPO switch, the companies will evaluate key communication performance -including packet loss, congestion control, and effective throughput- under workloads simulating distributed training and inference.

An exhibit related to this partnership and verification will be held at "KDDI SUMMIT 2026," the KDDI Group's largest business event, on October 27th and 28th (Venue: TAKANAWA GATEWAY Convention Center). Free pre-registration is required to attend. For details and registration, please visit the "KDDI SUMMIT 2026" special site (in Japanese only).

- (Note 1)Optical-Electronic Convergence (Optoelectronic Integration): A technology that combines electrical signals used for data processing with optical signals suitable for high-speed, high-capacity data transmission. By shortening the distance electrical signals travel and utilizing optical signals, the power required for communication is reduced.
- (Note 2)Co-Packaged Optics (CPO): A technology for achieving optical-electronic convergence. By placing the optical engine, which converts between electrical and optical signals, in close proximity to the switch chip that processes data, the distance electrical signals travel is shortened, thereby reducing power consumption.
- (Note 3)Tomahawk 6: Broadcom's latest Ethernet switch ASIC, delivering an industry-leading single-chip switching capacity of 102.4 Tbps.
- (Note 4) optical engine: A compact module integrating transmitting and receiving devices with the function of converting electrical signals to optical signals and vice versa.

- *The information contained in the articles is current at the time of publication.
Products, service fees, service content and specifications, contact information, and other details are subject to change without notice.
